source: Macronix MX25R6435F datasheet Rev. 1.6, August 08 2022 — section 15, ERASE AND PROGRAMMING PERFORMANCE, page 75
notes: Section 15 has two tables. Each mode caption sits ABOVE its table: the first table (64 KB block erase typ 0.8 s, page program typ 3.2 ms) is Ultra Low Power Mode, and the second (0.48 s / 0.85 ms) is High Performance Mode. Reading the captions as if they were below swaps the two, and they differ by 2-4x, so the swap changes every verdict.

The mode is Configuration Register-2 bit 1, the L/H switch. It is a VOLATILE bit whose power-on value comes from the part's ordering code, and Rev 1.6 no longer states a generic default (revision history, page 85: 'Removed L/H Switch bit descriptions (default value) P31'). Zephyr's nordic,qspi-nor driver does not write CR2, so a board runs whatever the part powers up as -- which makes the mode something to determine by measurement rather than to assume.

The '(Applied Vhv at WP# pin)' rows are a different operating condition, high voltage on WP#, and are recorded here only for completeness. They are not the basis of any comparison: nothing on the nRF5340-DK drives Vhv.

Typical figures are 25 C, typical VCC, checkerboard pattern for program and all-zero for erase. Maximum figures are 85 C at minimum operating voltage. A measurement at room temperature that sits well above typ is not out of spec, but it is worth explaining.

These are the part's internal erase and program times. They do not include the SPI bus time to shift the data in, nor the driver's per-call overhead -- both of which land in the model's fixed term, not its per-unit term. Compare per-unit against these; do not compare the fixed term against them.
